documents.title: Board Meeting Outcome for Outcome Of Meeting Of Executive Committee Of The Board Of Bhagyanagar India Limited Held On 13.08.2026 - Preferential Allotment Of Equity Shares
In-Principle Approval Under Regulation 28(1) Of SEBI ( LODR) Regulations, 2015
Corrigendum To Extra-Ordinary General Meeting ("EGM") Notice, Dated 30.06.2026
Submission Of Voting Results Along With Scrutinizer Report

analysis.summary: Bhagyanagar India Limited reported its Q1 FY27 earnings, highlighting a strong turnover of over 700 crores and an EBITDA margin of 5.43% driven by a temporary scrap supply shortage in April and May that allowed higher realizations. Management noted that June volumes normalized and projected volume growth of 12% to 15% for the full year, alongside ongoing corporate restructuring to form Tieramet Limited for the copper business. The company also announced a planned capex of 40 crores over FY27 and FY28, and a long-term revenue target of 5,000 crores by FY30. Bhagyanagar India Limited is a secondary copper player focused on value-added products for sectors like power, automotive, and solar. The company is undergoing a corporate restructuring involving the amalgamation of Bhagyanagar Copper Private Limited and the demerger of its copper business into Tieramet Ltd.

guidance.claim: The company expects to maintain its EBITDA margin between 5% and 5.5% for the rest of the year.
guidance.quote: Going forward in the year, we hope to maintain the EBITDA margin between 5% and 5.5%.

guidance.claim: Export contribution is estimated to be between 12% and 15% for the year.
guidance.quote: 12-15% would be a good estimate for the year.

guidance.claim: Management targets reaching 5,000 crores in revenue by FY30.
guidance.quote: So, see, the copper prices are out of our control. At 15% volume growth, you can do the reverse math based on the copper prices to see when we achieve it. But we are very confident of 5,000 crores by FY30, whatever the copper price.

demand_outlook.claim: India is projected to consume around 2.4 million metric tons of copper by 2030.
demand_outlook.quote: As we can see, India is actually one of the fastest growing copper users in the world, with around 2.4 million metric tons projected to be consumed in India by 2030.

demand_outlook.claim: Secondary copper demand in India is expected to double from 0.7 million metric tons to 1.4 million metric tons in the next 5 years.
demand_outlook.quote: Out of this, if you look at the secondary copper demand, it is expected to double in the next 5 years, from 0.7 million metric tons to 1.4 million metric tons.

demand_outlook.claim: The recycled copper market is estimated to grow at a CAGR of about 12% to 13% in India.
demand_outlook.quote: The recycled copper market, by some estimates, should be growing in India at a CAGR of about 12-13%.

demand_outlook.claim: The company expects the transition from primary to recycled copper in India to accelerate due to sustainability focus and supply constraints.
demand_outlook.quote: Growing sustainability focus and supply constraints are accelerating the transition from primary to recycled copper in India.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has finished adding a capacity of 35,000 metric tons which is now online.
capex_expansion.quote: We have also finished adding our capacity of 35,000 metric tons, which is online now.

capex_expansion.claim: Management has proposed a capex of 40 crores over the next 2 years (FY27 and FY28).
capex_expansion.quote: The management has proposed to do 40 crores of capex in the next 2 years, FY27 and FY28 and we are well on our way to achieve this.

capex_expansion.claim: A capacity expansion from 35,000 to 45,000 tons is projected for the next financial year between April and June.
capex_expansion.quote: So, this has been projected for the next financial year. The exact timelines are still not there, but as of now, our expectation is between April and June of next year; more likely June next year. From 35,000 to 45,000 tons.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved its highest EBITDA margin of recent times at 5.43% and highest PAT margin of 2.87% in Q1 FY27.
margins_costs.quote: We have had our highest EBITDA margin of recent times at 5.43%, our highest PAT margin of 2.87%.

margins_costs.claim: The higher EBITDA margin was driven by material shortages during trade route disruptions in the first two months.
margins_costs.quote: In the first two months, because of the disruption of all the trade routes and the shortage of material all over the country, while the turnover came down, we could take advantage of the situation by increasing our margins.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved its highest EBITDA per kg of 72 rupees in Q1 FY27.
margins_costs.quote: We have also had our highest share of value-added products sold this quarter, which is 63% and our highest EBITDA per kg of 72 rupees.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volumes for Q1 FY27 stood at 5,278 tons.
orders_capacity.quote: Our sales volumes have dropped, though; they have gone to 5,278 tons, which is a 9.5% decrease from the last quarter and a 6.5% decrease from last year.

orders_capacity.claim: Value-added products share reached its highest yet at 63% for the quarter.
orders_capacity.quote: We have achieved sales volumes of 5,200 tons. We have also had our highest share of value-added products sold this quarter, which is 63%

capital_allocation.claim: The company finalized the first round of fund raising at 52 crores to be received in August.
capital_allocation.quote: So, we have just finalized the first round of raising, at 52 crores, which is finalized, and the money should be in the bank in the month of August.

capital_allocation.claim: Projected debt in 2030 is estimated to be between 300 and 350 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: So, our projection is showing that between 300 and 350 crores will be our debt in 2030.

capital_allocation.claim: The company is raising Rs. 52.25 Crores through a preferential allotment of equity shares.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company acknowledges that forward-looking statements are subject to risks including economic performance, competition, and technological changes.
risks_headwinds.quote: These risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, the performance of the Indian economy and of the economies of various international markets, the performance of the industry in India and world-wide, competition, the Company's ability to successfully implement its strategy, the Company's future levels of growth and expansion, technological implementation, changes and advancements

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to complete the complete digital transformation of all processes and departments over the next year.
management_commitments.quote: Over the next year, we are going to do a complete digital transformation of our company, where every process, every department and all reporting will be completely digitalized automatically, and no manual entry would be required.

management_commitments.claim: The management proposes to execute 40 crores of capex over FY27 and FY28.
management_commitments.quote: The management has proposed to do 40 crores of capex in the next 2 years, FY27 and FY28 and we are well on our way to achieve this.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
